title: Turn a worm gear reducer over in a rollover fixture, lock it, and fit and screw down its output flange
instruction: Secure the gearbox in the rollover fixture, turn it over and lock it, then fit the output flange on its spigot and screw it down.
context: Team assemblers (O*NET 51-2092.00; about 1.4 million US workers) fit covers and flanges onto housings held in assembly fixtures and fasten them, a regular part of building gearboxes, pumps and motors; here it is a worm gear reducer's output flange. The hard parts are two-handed and order-bound. One hand carries the cradle over by its crank and holds it inside the lock bolt's narrow window (about 4 degrees) while the other pushes the bolt home. Then the flange, which starts turned 35 degrees, must be turned square to the face so that its four pre-fitted screws, whose tips are out of sight under it, drop into the tapped holes, and seated on the machined spigot without disturbing the gearbox. Only then is it screwed down: the locked fixture, not a hand, holds the work while one arm drives the screws. The fixture keeps the unit retained and square with the far face presented, and leaves both hands free for the part and the tool.
setup:
An assembly bench; mm; heights above the table; x from the arm bases' midpoint toward the work, y from the table's centre line (+y toward the left arm). The fixture is made from stock steel and aluminium plate and bar: every part is tabulated in the README and drawn in fixture_dimensions.svg; the screenshot shows the start.

Rollover fixture: two steel base plates 90 x 24 x 6 (y -156 to -132 and 32 to 56, x 195 to 285) joined by two 10 x 212 x 6 steel tie bars (x 150 to 160 and 320 to 330), fixed to the table (bolt the plates down on a real bench). On them two steel pillars 60 wide (x 210 to 270), 12 thick: the near one y -150 to -138, 90 tall; the far one y 38 to 50, 125 tall, with a 12 mm gap 102 to 114 high for the bolt. A horizontal axle along y at x 240, 78 high, carries an aluminium cradle that turns from level (its start, resting on its near stop) to a far stop at 195 degrees: two rails 6 thick, inner faces 100 apart, y -130 to 20, 44 to 121.5 high; two 5 mm ledges 44 to 49 high, x 190 to 194 and 269 to 290, y -70 to -5; a near stop plate y -87.5 to -80; a far end plate 100 wide, y 20 to 30, 33 to 123 high, with a notch 16 wide and 30 tall open at its bottom edge. A dark steel crank, 60 from the axle, carries a yellow plastic knob sleeve 30 x 24 x 40 (y -194 to -170) that turns freely on its pin; the knob starts level with the axle at x 180.

A blue aluminium retaining bar 99 x 30 x 8 (113.5 to 121.5 high), with a lug 40 wide up to 153 high on its crank side, slides 67.5 along y between the rails, from parked (y -120 to -90) to closed (y -52.5 to -22.5), 4 mm over the gearbox's upper spigot. A red aluminium lock bolt 12 x 12 x 56 (y 36 to 92 withdrawn), 108 high in the far pillar's gap, lug top 150, slides 15 toward -y; it enters the notch only within about 4 degrees of turned over, else the plate stops it after 6 mm.

Gearbox: a Motovario NMRV 030 worm gear reducer without motor, die-cast aluminium, painted grey, 1.2 kg (maker's catalogue): centre distance 30, 63 hub to hub, output faces 29 from the output axis, 55 h8 locating spigots 2.5 high, 14 bore, four M6 x 11 tapped holes on a 65 circle at 45 degrees in each output face; about 97 x 95 x 63 overall. It lies in the cradle with output face J (its spigot painted orange) down on the ledges, output axis vertical at x 231.5, y -37.5, feet toward the arms, input flange toward +y.

Output flange (the maker's type FA flange for size 030, catalogue p. 71; aluminium, 0.13 kg): a 70 x 70 x 6 plate, a 54 neck and a 50 x 4 spigot, 25.5 tall; under it a 3 deep recess for the housing's spigot. Four M6 x 16 socket head cap screws (ISO 14579, TX 30 drive, black oxide) come pre-fitted in its holes (a kitting step; no thread engaged), tips 1 proud and heads 9 above the plate; once the flange is seated each tip rests in its tapped hole's mouth with no thread engaged, and seated a screw has 10 of thread in its 11 deep hole: 9 turns at the M6 pitch of 1. It sits turned 35 degrees anticlockwise (seen from above) from the angle at which its screws line up with the tapped holes, on a steel kitting post 50 across and 60 tall at x 150, y 150.

Screwdriver: a Wera 367 TORX Stubby TX 30 x 25, article 05008861001 (blade 25 long, 5.6 across; Kraftform handle 54 long, 34 across at its widest; 37 g), drawn in its real shape and colours; it collides as its blade and a 29 mm cylinder over the handle. It stands handle up in a dark 40 x 40 x 40 holster with a 12 mm bore at x 335, y -200.
scoring: Read at the end of the run. A hand is a gripper's fingertip midpoint; let go means both hands 6 cm or more from the part's box. 0 for good if the cradle turns past 30 degrees without the gearbox in it under the closed bar, or if the gearbox or the flange leaves the table. Gearbox in: its output axis within 5 mm along and across the cradle of where it started, 1 mm below to 5.5 mm above that in the cradle's axes (it rests on the bar once turned), tilted under 10 degrees. Bar closed: 62.5 mm or more of travel. Turned over: within 6 degrees of 180. Bolt home: 12 mm or more of travel. Flange seated: every corner of its housing face within 0.5 mm of face J and its centre within 1 mm of the output axis (it can only seat with all four screw tips in the tapped holes). A screw is down when its head is within 0.5 mm of the flange, it was then turned on 15 degrees or more against the thread's 0.5 N m snug resistance, and every tightening turn it got was made with the bolt home. Lift test: once all four are down, hands clear and all at rest for 1 s, the task file pulls the flange straight up, ramped to 10 N over 0.5 s and held 1 s; it passes if the flange lifts 0.5 mm or less, and runs again if anything moves afterwards. Score: 0.25 gearbox in and bar closed; 0.5 also turned over and bolt home; 0.75 also the flange seated and let go; 0.9 also two diagonally opposite screws down; 1.0 all four down, the lift test passed, both hands 6 cm or more from the flange, the driver, the knob and the bolt's lug, and all at rest (parts under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s, cradle under 3 deg/s, bar and bolt under 1 cm/s) for the last 1 s. Real trial: tape and protractor for the fixture, a 0.1 mm feeler at the flange's corners and under each head, a 10 N spring scale hooked under the flange's neck; snug: the video shows each screw turned on after its head is down, and 10 N on the spring scale 50 mm out on a TX 30 L-key (0.5 N m) does not turn it further; the flange's centring follows from its recess sitting over the spigot (no gap at the corners).
reset_notes: Set the cradle level, withdraw the bar and bolt, back the four screws out to 1 mm proud, and put the flange on its post and the screwdriver in its holster. The gearbox stays in the cradle. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. Thread not simulated: while the bit sits square in a socket, the driver's turn runs that screw along its hole 1 mm a turn (M6 x 1), 9 turns from its tip resting in the hole's mouth; the thread resists the driver 0.15 N m running, 0.5 N m once the head is down (estimates). Final torque (about 10 N m by tables) is a later station. A fixed joint holds each pre-fitted screw until its thread catches (kitting). Fits loose. Drawn as the real parts; collision shapes simpler.
